name: Slagside Ironhand Welding Gauntlet
description:
Heavy split-leather gauntlets reinforced with ceramic fiber panels across the knuckles and dorsal hand, stitched in double-pass aramid thread. The wrist cuffs are wide and buckled with reclaimed steel hardware, scorched amber-brown from repeated heat exposure. Most pairs show carbon streaks and flux spatter that no cleaning removes — worn like a badge.

Lining is a single layer of reflective fiberglass batting, functional but unrefined. The thumb and index finger are reinforced with additional ceramic tile insets for arc-strike resistance. Sold in pairs, often resold individually on Shelf markets.
functionality: Rated for arc welding and open-flame exposure up to 900°C brief contact. Wide cuff protects the forearm gap common in aug-compatible sleeves. No haptic or electronic components — fully passive thermal protection.
what_it_says: This person works with fire and doesn't complain about it.
story_hooks: A pair of these gloves is found at a crime scene — the wearer left behind no prints, but the ceramic dust matches a specific batch sold only to one Shelf fabricator.
A Tier 3 inspector arrives at a factory floor and notices a worker's Slagside gauntlets have been modified with a hidden wire channel — someone's routing signal through the cuff.
